tasks.title: Verify the scheduled-jobs story against django.tasks gaps
tasks.endGoal: The project has a demonstrated, documented pattern for recurring and delayed work: deadline-as-data (e.g. expires_at) + an idempotent sweep management command that goes through services; a cadence trigger per environment (local = manual/compose loop, prod = external scheduler); a cleanup command that prunes finished task-result rows.
tips: django.tasks core (Django 6.0) provides API only - NO worker, NO retries, NO delayed execution (run_after absent from core), NO periodic tasks, NO delivery guarantees, NO monitoring dashboard. Each gap needs a named owner in this repo.
Worker = the django-tasks reference package's DB backend + db_worker (`just worker`); in prod it is a separate long-running service deployed in lockstep with web so task code never drifts.

Sweep pattern (decided 2026-07-18): never schedule one event per row - store the deadline on the model, filter reads on it so correctness never depends on the scheduler, and let a frequent idempotent sweep materialize the state. Side-effectful closes go row-by-row through the owning service, not bulk update().
Sweep commands live in apps/<app>/management/commands (layering: management -> services); recurring cadence changes are infrastructure-only edits, new jobs = new command + new schedule entry.
JSON-only task args (tuples become lists, no datetimes/models) - the existing pk-strings rule already complies; keep return values JSON-safe or return nothing.
No timeouts / rate limits / uniqueness in the framework: guard in the task body (select_for_update, status checks) where duplicate or hung execution would hurt.

tasks.title: Write the AWS deployment runbook (ECS Express Mode + worker + schedules)
tasks.endGoal: docs/ contains a runbook covering: web tier via ECS Express Mode (ECR image, execution + infrastructure roles, containerPort, health-check path, env/secrets, task role for S3/SES), worker as a plain ECS service on the same cluster, EventBridge Scheduler entries kept in IaC for every cron job, and the explicit note that DB/Redis are outside Express Mode's scope.
tips: Express Mode facts (researched 2026-07-18): HTTPS URL https://<name>.ecs.<region>.on.aws, ALB auto-shared across up to 25 services with same networking, canary deploys + 5XX rollback alarm (strategy not changeable), defaults 1 vCPU/2GB, target-tracking 60% CPU min 1/max 20 tasks, no extra charge - pay for Fargate/ALB/CloudWatch/transfer.

Custom task definitions supported since July 2026: container must be named 'Main' with a single TCP port mapping and FARGATE compatibility; taskDefinitionArn is mutually exclusive with primaryContainer/cpu/memory/role params. Never rename the Main container - it breaks Express Mode updates.

First Express service in a VPC pins the shared ALB's subnets/AZs - create with subnets from ALL AZs. Public subnets -> internet-facing ALB + public task IPs; private subnets -> internal ALB (bring your own NAT).
Custom domain is not first-class: manual ACM cert + host-header listener rule on the shared ALB + Route 53 record.
IaC: Terraform aws_ecs_express_gateway_service (provider >= 6.23.0); CloudFormation/CDK supported since launch. Schedules live in IaC next to the commands they trigger - never click-ops.
Recurring jobs: EventBridge Scheduler -> ECS RunTask with command override `python manage.py <command>` reusing the task definition family; one-off Fargate seconds per run, no always-on beat process.
AWS positions Express Mode as the migration target for App Runner (availability changing) and the EOL Copilot CLI - a point in favor of betting on it.
